X1.name: recursive backtracking
X1.mech: Extend the current path one cell at a time by recursion, marking only the cells that are on the current path; when stuck, undo the last step (unmark that cell) and try the next direction.
X1.pseudo:
1. if start or goal is a wall, return []
2. path = []; on_path = empty set
3. extend(cell): append cell to path and add it to on_path
4.     if cell is goal, return true
5.     for each free neighbour n of cell that is not in on_path: if extend(n) returns true, return true
6.     remove cell from path and from on_path (so that other routes may use it again); return false
7. if extend(start) returns true, return path; otherwise return []

X2.name: the Floyd-Warshall algorithm
X2.mech: Treat every free cell as a node and fill a table of distances between every pair of nodes by allowing each node in turn as an intermediate stop; then read the path from start to goal out of the table.
X2.pseudo:
1. if start or goal is a wall, return []
2. cells = list of all free cells; n = its length; idx = position of each cell in the list
3. dist = n x n table of infinity; nxt = n x n table of None; dist[i][i] = 0; for adjacent cells i, j: dist[i][j] = 1 and nxt[i][j] = j
4. for k in 0..n-1: for i in 0..n-1: for j in 0..n-1:
5.     if dist[i][k] + dist[k][j] < dist[i][j]: dist[i][j] = dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]; nxt[i][j] = nxt[i][k]
6. s = idx[start]; g = idx[goal]; if s != g and nxt[s][g] is None, return []
7. path = [start]; while s != g: s = nxt[s][g]; append cells[s] to path
8. return path
